claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm−3.
Al is a low-density alloying element suitable for reducing the density of HfMoTaTiZr.
Introducing a small amount of Al into HfMoTaTiZr will reduce its overall density.
Al addition will not significantly compromise the strength of HfMoTaTiZr at room temperature or elevated temperatures up to approximately 1000 °C.
Al addition will maintain the ductility of HfMoTaTiZr at room temperature and elevated temperatures.
The added Al will form a solid solution with the existing elements in HfMoTaTiZr.
Solid-solution strengthening caused by Al will maintain the alloy's mechanical properties.
Vacuum arc melting is a feasible fabrication method for HfMoTaTiZr.
An appropriate post-casting heat treatment can be used for the proposed Al-modified HfMoTaTiZr.
The mechanical-property evaluation should cover room temperature through 1000 °C.
Compression and tension are applicable loading modes for evaluating the proposed alloy.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has strong room-temperature mechanical performance and has been evaluated at elevated temperatures.
The hypothesis can be tested by fabricating HfMoTaTiZr alloys with varying Al additions and measuring density, microstructure, and mechanical properties at room and elevated temperatures.
A significant degradation of strength or ductility at room temperature or elevated temperature after Al addition would falsify the hypothesis.
